facts.text: On this date in 1520, Magellan's fleet became the first to exit the strait now bearing his name into the Pacific — a passage so brutal that three of his five ships had already mutinied or turned back.
On this date in 1943, Roosevelt, Churchill, and Stalin met in Tehran for the first Allied summit — Stalin had refused to travel farther, so the others flew to him.
Manila is the world's most densely populated city proper, packing over 70,000 people per square kilometer — denser than any borough of New York or any district of Tokyo.
More people live inside a 4,000km circle centered on Bangladesh than live outside it — that single circle contains over half the Earth's entire population.
Canada is larger than the entire European Union by land area, yet holds fewer people than the state of California.
On this day in 1954, the Dow Jones closed at 382 — a level it had last hit in 1929. It took 25 years for the market to simply break even after the Great Crash.
On this day in 1895, the first American car race was held from Chicago to Evanston. The winner averaged 7.3 mph. The prize was $2,000 — roughly $72,000 today.

The NYSE was once nearly purchased by a single man. In 1929, during the crash, Richard Whitney strode onto the floor and bought U.S. Steel at a price above market to halt the panic. He later went to Sing Sing for embezzlement.
Saudi Aramco's 2019 IPO raised $25.6 billion — the largest in history — yet the company sold less than 2% of itself. The world's most profitable business barely needed the money.
The entire global bond market is roughly $140 trillion. That dwarfs equities — yet most retail investors have never bought a single bond in their lives.
On this date in 1967, astronomers Jocelyn Bell and Antony Hewish detected the first pulsar — a neutron star spinning 30 times per second, so precise it was briefly mistaken for alien contact.
Your skeleton is not static. Almost every atom in your bones is replaced over roughly a decade, meaning the skeleton you were born with no longer exists.
On this date in 1520, Magellan's fleet entered the Pacific through the strait now bearing his name — and found an ocean so vast it took 98 days to cross without sight of land.
A neutron star packs more mass than the Sun into a sphere the size of a city. A teaspoon of its material would weigh roughly a billion tons on Earth.
The human eye can detect a single photon of light in complete darkness. Your visual system is operating at the absolute physical limit of sensitivity.
On this day in 1520, Magellan's fleet became the first to exit the strait now bearing his name into the Pacific — he called it 'Mar Pacífico' because after the brutal passage, it seemed calm.
Oxford University was already 300 years old when the Aztec Empire was founded. Europe's oldest university predates the civilization Cortés would destroy by three centuries.
On this day in 1942, the Cocoanut Grove fire in Boston killed 492 people and directly revolutionized burn treatment, skin grafting, and disaster triage in American medicine.
Cleopatra lived closer in time to the Moon landing than to the construction of the Great Pyramid. She and Neil Armstrong are separated by 2,000 years; she and Khufu by 2,500.

The fax machine was invented in 1843 — before the American Civil War, before the telephone, before electric light. We treat it as obsolete office furniture, but it's older than almost everything in the modern world.

Today in 1520, Magellan's fleet entered the Pacific — which he named 'Mar Pacífico' for its deceptive calm. The Portuguese word 'pacífico' descends from Latin 'pax,' peace, encoding a sailor's relief into geography itself.

Today in 1680, Gian Lorenzo Bernini died, leaving a language richer: 'chiaroscuro,' the Italian word for the dramatic interplay of light and shadow, literally means 'bright-dark' — a noun built from two opposites holding each other.

Mamihlapinatapai: a Yaghan word from Tierra del Fuego meaning the wordless look shared by two people who both want something but neither will initiate. Linguists cite it as one of the most concise expressions of human ambivalence ever coined.

The Japanese word '木漏れ日' (komorebi) names sunlight filtering through leaves — a phenomenon so specific it has no single-word equivalent in English, yet anyone who has walked through a forest has felt it completely.

Sonder, coined by John Koenig in 'The Dictionary of Obscure Sorrows,' describes realizing every passerby has a life as vivid as your own. Its adoption into common usage shows how quickly a named feeling becomes a felt one.
On this day in 2017, Bitcoin crossed $10,000 for the first time — then hit $11,000 within 24 hours. The entire move from $1K to $11K had taken less than eleven months.
On this day in 2022, BlockFi filed for bankruptcy, listing FTX as its largest creditor. It had accepted a $400M credit facility from FTX just five months earlier as a lifeline.
Ethereum's gas limit is not hardcoded — miners and validators vote it up or down each block, nudging it by 1/1024th at a time. It has grown roughly 10x since genesis without a hard fork.
The Bitcoin genesis block contains the headline 'Chancellor on brink of second bailout for banks' — not as metadata but embedded in the coinbase transaction field, permanently unalterable.

Satoshi's known wallet addresses have never moved a single satoshi. The roughly 1.1 million BTC mined in Bitcoin's first year sits untouched, making Satoshi one of the largest holders by complete inaction.

Today in history: On Nov 28, 1994, Checkers/Dark Thought became the first computer to defeat a human grandmaster at chess in a tournament game — three years before Deep Blue's famous 1997 match got all the credit.
Today in history: On Nov 28, 2022, ChatGPT launched publicly. It reached 1 million users in 5 days — a pace that took Netflix 3.5 years and Facebook 10 months.
GPT-4's training run is estimated to have consumed roughly 50 gigawatt-hours of electricity — enough to power about 4,600 US homes for a year, for a single training pass.
The 2009 Netflix Prize was won by an ensemble of 107 models. Netflix never deployed it — the engineering cost outweighed the accuracy gain, a lesson the field keeps relearning.

Transformers were introduced in 2017 by researchers who expected them to improve machine translation. Within 5 years the architecture had displaced CNNs in computer vision, protein folding, and audio synthesis.
